## Critique
- claim-1: The bounded excerpt directly defines \(I_{r,n-r}\) as the Schur-span outside \((n-r)^r\) and states that it is an ideal. The grounding is exact and sufficient.
- claim-2: The cited excerpt directly supplies the quotient isomorphism and the surviving Schur indexing by partitions inside \((n-r)^r\). No adjacent result is substituted.
- claim-3: This follows formally from claim-1 because the Schur functions form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(\Lambda\): quotienting by the span of the complementary basis subset leaves the indicated free basis. Renaming \(n-r=q\) is harmless. The requested target is established.
